questions.markdown: Write a simple Java program for the Weather Monitoring System. The system should enable users to add weather data, including temperature, humidity for different cities identified by unique IDs. Users should be able to view the weather details for all recorded locations, update the weather data. Additionally, the system should alert users if the temperature exceeds a specified threshold. Use the switch case to do the operations.

Demonstrate a Java program for the Vaccination Tracking System to manage individuals' vaccination statuses by collecting essential details such as name, ID, severe allergy status (as a boolean), and the date of the last vaccination. The system checks everyone's eligibility for the next vaccination based on two criteria: they must not have severe allergies and must have waited at least six months since their last vaccination. The program uses an array of vaccine objects to store and process this information efficiently, providing a structured way to track vaccinations.

Write a program that accepts a string (with all alphabets in lower-case) as a command-line argument. Display this string along with its length on the console. Identify any vowel(s) in the string and convert it to upper case without making use of any in-built functions. Also, display the final converted string back on the console.

Write a Java program using inheritance and interfaces to design a Payment Processing System for an e-commerce platform that supports multiple payment methods such as Credit Cards and PayPal. The system also needs to handle transaction logging and user notifications.

- All payment methods share common functionalities like payment validation and refunds.
- Different payment methods should have their own specific ways to process payments.
- Logging and notification should be optional features, as not all payment methods require these functionalities

Provide code examples to demonstrate how inheritance is used for general payment processing and how interfaces are applied for optional features like logging and notifications.
Write a generic method to swap any two values of any type of data and display the values after swapping. With suitable examples illustrate generic restrictions on arrays.

Assume that you are tasked to develop a library system where different classes reside in separate packages. In the package `library.books`, a class `Book` is defined with the following attributes: title (public), author (protected), isbn (default), and price (private). Another package `library.users` contains a class `Member` that needs to access the `Book` class attributes and print their values.

1) Explain which attributes of the `Book` class can be accessed directly in the `Member` class and why.
2) Write a code snippet to demonstrate how the `Member` class in the `library.users` package can access the accessible attributes of the `Book` class.

Create a class `Book` that encapsulates book details - ISBN and genre of a book at a library. The different genres that the library offers for its readers is stored in a string array, `genres` which is a variable within `IGenre` interface. Create a class `BookDemo` with `main()` that initializes an array of `Book` objects. All the books must be checked if they can be procured from library or not through `checkGenre(Book[] b)` of `Book`. A book cannot be procured if its specified genre is not in `genres` array. Handle this scenario by throwing `GenreUnavailableException` that displays a suitable message such as "Genre: Sci-Fi of Book:103 not available".

Build a Java program that uses Runnable Interface with the following functionality: The 1D array (size of the array be a square number, ex: 9, 16, 25 etc) is taken from the user in main(). Create one child thread to sort the elements and another child thread to create the 2D array (square matrix) from the sorted array. Display the size of the matrix in the main().
Write a Java program that demonstrates thread communication between two threads using `wait()` and `notify()` to display the number and its square alternately. Consider numbers from 1 to 10.

Develop a generic class `Pair< T, U>` that can store two elements of any type, one of type `T` and the other of type `U`. Implement the following functionalities:

a) A constructor to initialize the two elements.
b) Methods to retrieve the first element (`getFirst()`) and the second element (`getSecond()`).
c) Methods to update the values of the first element (`setFirst()`) and the second element (`setSecond()`).
d) A static generic method `swap()` that accepts two `Pair` objects of the same type and swaps their values.

Build a java program using thread synchronization concept based on this scenario. Indian railway wants to develop an application to book 1 AC tickets for the travellers whose total count is 10. Consider that you have been assigned to develop the module for ticket booking wherein you are required to create 3 threads using the class named `ACTRAINBOOKING` by extending the `Thread` class. Further inside the run method call the method booking method which is used to book the seats and display appropriate message about the status of booking. (if tickets are not available display message and do not book it). This method booking is defined inside another class named `bookseat` which has instance variable named count whose value is assigned to 10 which represents the number of seats.
